exposure: albumin level (mild hypoproteinemia vs severe hypoproteinemia)
outcome: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit occupancy rate
finding: Severe hypoproteinemia preeclampsia was associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including earlier gestational age at delivery, severe hypertension, abnormal liver and renal function, ascites, abruption, cesarean section, fetal growth restriction, and higher Neonatal Intensive Care Unit occupancy rate, compared to mild hypoproteinemia preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Women with severe hypoproteinemia preeclampsia had a higher rate of cesarean section than those with mild hypoproteinemia preeclampsia.
